subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLOs & GPU sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity performance validation (recap + next steps)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- Primary SLOs you called out: 95th percentile token latency (streaming token latency) target <= 120ms, end-to-end response latency (for typical 512-token responses) <= 450ms.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~200 concurrent requests during peak; burst concurrency up to 350 for short windows.
- Target steady throughput: ~250–300 requests/sec (avg request size ~350 tokens).
- Streaming required for real-time user experience; partial responses should begin within 100–150ms.
- Model family: you mentioned Mistral-variant fine-tuned for summarization; estimate avg tokens generated ~350.

Proposed next steps:
1) We run a dedicated capacity performance validation (4–7 day window) to size GPUs and reserved throughput to meet the SLOs.
2) Redwood will provide a test harness and recommended load config (attached). Please confirm a representative test prompt set and a sandbox dataset for realism.
3) Rafael (cc’ed) will propose GPU topology options (H100 vs A100) and reserved throughput numbers.
4) We schedule an engineering kick-off + canary run the week of Nov 30. Please confirm availability for a 30-min sync.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-validation-plan.pdf (validation plan), loadtest-config.yaml (recommended load profile).

Questions for you before we start:
- Can you confirm peak concurrent connections and whether batching is acceptable for any subset of requests?
- Are there any strict compliance/network constraints we should know about for the sandbox environment?

Thanks — I’ll wait for your availability and the test prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0186

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity performance validation (recap + next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding a few clarifications: 

Confirmed SLOs / workload:
- 95th percentile token latency target (streaming): <= 120ms.
- End-to-end p95 for 512-token outputs: target <= 450ms.
- Average request: 350 tokens input, ~350 tokens generation.
- Steady-state: 250 req/s; peak bursts up to 340 req/s for 2–5 minute windows.
- Concurrent connections: ~200 persistent streaming clients; spikes up to 370.

Other constraints:
- Streaming latency is critical — partial chunks must start arriving within 100–150ms.
- We prefer single-region deployment in us-west1; data cannot leave the region for this project.
- We have strict audit logging requirements (SOC 2 scope) — we’ll need request-level audit logs for the validation runs.

Test dataset: I’ll upload a representative prompt set (500 prompts) to the drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

One ask: can you provide an early estimate of GPU sizing (H100 vs A100) for the stated targets so we can budget before the validation? Even a ballpark is helpful.

Samir
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme AI
samir.khan@acme.ai
\---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity performance validation (recap + next steps)

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Samir. Ballpark sizing and proposed validation plan below. Rafael and Aditya are looped in to scope the hands-on run.

Ballpark GPU sizing (high-level):
- H100 (PCIe/HBM): for your workload (avg 350 gen tokens, streaming priority, p95 token latency <=120ms) we estimate 3–5 H100s for steady 250 req/s with room for bursts, depending on model optimizations/quantization. H100 gives better per-GPU throughput for large context and streaming.
- A100 (80GB): comparable throughput would likely require ~5–8 A100s for the same SLOs (depends on optimized kernels / batch sizes).
- Notes: exact numbers vary with model variant, quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit), and whether we can leverage batch packing and KV cache reuse for high overlap requests.

Proposed validation run (attached plan):
- Phase 1 (baseline): single-GPU microbenchmarks (latency per token, memory, warmup) — 1 day.
- Phase 2 (sizing): run scaled load tests on 1, 3, 5, and 7 GPU topologies (both H100 and A100 flavors) — 2 days.
- Phase 3 (reserved throughput & canary): provision a dedicated pool with the recommended topology + reserved throughput enforcement, run 24–48 hour soak with production-like traffic plus bursts — 2 days.
- Phase 4 (reporting): p50/p95/p99 latency, token latency traces, failure modes, and cost-per-token projection for reserved capacity — 1 day.

Operational items:
- Redwood will enable request-level audit logs during the run; we’ll provide an export to your secure bucket.
- We’ll run the load tests inside your preferred us-west1 region.
- Please confirm network/VPN access details and whether we should use a customer-managed bastion for the sandbox.

Next steps:
1) Rafael — can you propose the specific machine sizes (H100 SKU, A100 SKU), reserved throughput numbers (tokens/sec and concurrent request limit per pool), and a suggested canary schedule?
2) Samir — confirm the test prompt set upload and availability for a 30-min kickoff on Nov 30 or Dec 1.

I’ve attached the validation plan and the loadtest config we’ll use as a starting point.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
\---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity performance validation (recap + next steps)

Hi all — quick technical notes and concrete numbers to prepare the validation: 

Suggested topologies (initial proposal):
- Option A (H100 optimized): 4 x H100 (NVIDIA H100 SXM or comparable cloud SKU) in a single pool. Reserved throughput: target 320 req/s steady (to cover headroom), token throughput target ~112k tokens/sec aggregated. Concurrent connection limit: 400. Expected p95 token latency: ~80–110ms (depends on quantization).
- Option B (A100): 6 x A100 (80GB) in a single pool. Reserved throughput: 320 req/s steady; token throughput ~96k tokens/sec aggregated. Concurrent connection limit: 400. Expected p95 token latency: ~120–160ms.

Reserved throughput strategy:
- We recommend setting reserved throughput at 85% of validated max sustained throughput per pool to ensure headroom. During canary we’ll enforce soft limits then hard limits if SLA breach occurs.

Streaming config notes:
- Use chunk size 32 tokens for streaming chunks to balance first-byte latency and overhead.
- Prefer frame-based sending (partial responses) so UX starts at first chunk (~80–120ms).

Test artifacts and links:
- Load test config: loadtest-config.yaml (attached).
- Test harness: https://app.redwood.ai/tests/ACME-2026-DED-01

Operational ask for validation run:
- Provide test prompt set (500 prompts) in the drive folder.
- Temporary service account with write access to your audit log bucket for exports.
- Network egress rule to allow traffic from our validation fleet in us-west1.

I’ll be online for the kickoff on Nov 30 — propose 11:00am PST. If Samir can confirm, we’ll lock the slot and provision the H100 option for the canary; we can run the A100 comparison as part of Phase 2.

-Rafael
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
